statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 6 after an orderly, mid-range cash close, while stress firms to 72 in the high band on crude at six-week highs, a 10-year at the top of its range and an unresolved US-Iran tanker conflict.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour: the Nasdaq-100 closed 107 points above its session low after a gradual two-sided fade, and no repeated extension after a failed retracement was observed at any point in the session. Cross-asset channels are firm but conflicting, which raises stress rather than tail. The narrow flagged window covers the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen after the daily maintenance halt, where any headline accumulated during the pause is repriced in a single gap into thin liquidity.
headline: NDX closes at 29,507.70, down 0.12% and well off its low, as a 1.18% Dow decline, WTI at $93.97 and a 4.806% 10-year keep stress high while two-sided trade holds tail at 6
body: The US cash session has closed and the assessment now rests on verified closing levels rather than on an in-progress price path. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 29,507.70, down 36.45 points or 0.12%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 day range and just under the 29,544.15 prior close. That close sits 107 points above the session low and 148 points below the high, in the lower half of the range but nowhere near either extreme. Nasdaq-100 futures trade near 29,525.25, down 0.14%, inside a 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 range, leaving price roughly 240 points under the futures high; a second reading from Investing.com shows 29,535.00 within the same range, so the level is corroborated. The path into the close was a gradual, two-sided fade of roughly fifty points per hour off the high rather than a directional leg, and at no point in the session was repeated extension after a failed retracement observed. That is the direct opposite of the structure that overwhelms a mean-reversion basket, which is why tail eases to 6 even as the surrounding channels firm. Index internals were unusually dispersed, which is the reason the dominant mode stays mixed rather than trend-down. The Dow closed 628.18 points lower at 52,786.07, a 1.18% decline, the S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,673.52, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.32% to 26,421.41, and the Nasdaq-100 lost only 0.12%. Within the index, semiconductors led decisively while megacaps lagged: Intel gained about 9% on reported price increases, AMD about 5.9%, Arm about 3.7%, Qualcomm about 3.2% on its multi-generational custom-silicon agreement with Amazon Web Services, and Broadcom about 3.0%, against declines of roughly 2.0% in Nvidia and 1.1% in both Apple and Microsoft. Application software fell about 3.5% on AI-displacement concerns. A 5-point spread between the Dow and the Nasdaq-100 in percentage-of-move terms, with leadership rotating inside the index rather than the index moving as one, is dispersion, not index-level one-way pressure. Volatility firmed without becoming disorderly. VIX stands at 15.75, up 2.94%, inside a 15.22 to 15.94 day range; it is in the upper part of that range but remains low in absolute terms and far from a level consistent with a disorderly tape. The rates channel is the firmer of the two macro amplifiers: the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.806%, up about two basis points, at the top of its 4.760 to 4.812 range and, per contemporaneous reporting, near a two-decade high. A yield printing at session highs into the close is a genuine stress amplifier for long-duration technology, but it did not translate into one-way equity pressure during the session. Energy remains the largest single contributor to the elevated stress reading. WTI is near $93.97, up about 2.72% and at a six-week high, with Brent testing the high $90s and reported as approaching $100. The driver is an active maritime conflict rather than a demand story: the United States and Iran have exchanged strikes on shipping, with US forces disabling or destroying three Iranian tankers after Iranian ballistic-missile launches toward US warships near the Strait of Hormuz, and the IRGC navy warning vessels against transiting unauthorised routes. Marine traffic data cited in coverage shows only about thirteen vessels crossing the strait daily. Iran's parliament speaker has stated that the era of proportionate responses is over. This is an unresolved discontinuity channel that could reprice overnight, and it is the principal reason the flagged window sits at the futures reopen rather than in the current hour. Two further channels stay open. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about $20 billion of US goods took effect and remain in force, escalating the North American trade dispute. Rate expectations have turned hawkish: following the strong August payrolls report, CME FedWatch pricing cited in contemporaneous reporting puts the probability of a 25 basis-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC near 58%, a marked shift from the roughly 70% probability of no change priced before the recent Federal Reserve commentary. Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI are the next two inputs into that pricing and both sit inside the seven-day calendar. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 20:20 UTC, roughly ten minutes before this assessment, with collection status ok, complete coverage and no warnings, so it is treated as fresh supporting context. It corroborates the independent research rather than replacing it: index futures show NQ -0.15% against ES -0.57% and YM -1.18%, confirming the dispersion; VX +2.36% and CL +2.80% confirm the volatility and energy channels; the full 2s-to-30s Treasury futures complex is lower, confirming the yield rise; megacaps show only two of eight positive with 1.98 percentage points of dispersion, while semiconductors show five of seven positive with a 3.02% mean. As required, this delayed latest-session context is used only as cross-asset confirmation and never as evidence of live NQ price-path structure. The narrow flagged window covers 21:55 to 22:30 UTC. CME index futures halt from 21:00 to 22:00 UTC, so any headline arriving during that hour is stored rather than priced and is then released into a single gap at the reopen. With an active tanker conflict and crude at six-week highs, that reopen into thin liquidity is the horizon's most credible discontinuity instant, and it is deliberately narrow rather than a broad overnight flag.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band without interruption. Tail ran between 5 and 10 from Monday evening through Tuesday morning, stepped up to 15 in the 14:00 UTC slot on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back through 8, 7 and 6 as that leg was fully retraced, and finished the session at 8 through the power hour. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to a peak of 72 in early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect, eased to the high 60s through the afternoon, and firmed again to 71 into the close as crude pressed to six-week highs. The dominant mode was mixed for most of the window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, sat at normal through the quiet Monday evening hours, and turned to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens with the cash close already printed, orderly and mid-range, and conditional tail eased to 6. It falls to the horizon floor of 5 during the 21:00 UTC CME maintenance halt, when no price path can form, then steps to the overnight peak of 9 at the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, which is the flagged window and the horizon's narrowest genuine discontinuity checkpoint given the active US-Iran tanker conflict. Conditional tail then settles between 6 and 7 through the Asian session, lifts to 8 at the 07:00 UTC European cash open, and holds in the 7 to 8 range through the European morning and the US pre-market. The horizon peak of 13 falls in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full hour after Wednesday's US cash open, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion; nothing about that structure is observed, and Tuesday's equivalent slot reached 15 before fully retracing. Scores then decay through midday before lifting to 10 at the 17:00 UTC pairing of Apple's confirmed product keynote and the US 10-year note auction, closing the horizon at 9 through the Wednesday power hour. All 24 slots stay inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where the tanker conflict is active and Hormuz transit is heavily constrained; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect; and rate expectations, with roughly 58% priced for a September hike ahead of Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels resolves inside the horizon, while confidence decays overnight as the evidence base gathered around the close ages and recovers once Wednesday's cash session provides fresh observable structure.
